title: Credential Lifecycle — Gate
description: The other half of the conformance pair: a single credential-gated action that accepts or refuses a presentation. The conformance run submits to this gate after every status change, so the gate's verdict — not the wallet's own status field — is what proves each status is actually enforced. FailClosed by design: an unresolvable status must refuse, never pass.
author: Sorcha Team

template.title: Credential Lifecycle — Gate
template.description: One action, one credential requirement. Kept to a single terminal action deliberately: the conformance run submits to it many times, and anything that had to be cleaned up or advanced between submissions would make the runs interfere with each other.

metadata.features: Credential Gate, Trust Policy, FailClosed Revocation

participants.name: Credential Holder
participants.description: Presents the credential. Pre-bound deliberately: a conformance check wants the fewest variables, so the holder is known at setup and the credential requirement is the only thing that can cause a refusal.

participants.name: Relying Party
participants.description: Receives the outcome of the presentation. Present because a blueprint requires at least two participants, and because a gate with nobody on the other side is not a gate — but deliberately given NO action of its own, so the conformance run never has to advance an instance between submissions.

actions.title: Present Credential
actions.description: Holder presents the conformance credential. Terminal on success. The sender is pre-bound, so every refusal the conformance run asserts is attributable to this action's credential requirement and nothing else.

phase.title: Conformance phase
phase.description: Which lifecycle phase submitted this — active / suspended / reinstated / revoked. Recorded so a failed run can be read back from the ledger.

credentialRequirements.description: Requires a conformance credential from the authority whose status is not set for any purpose. FailClosed: an unresolvable status refuses rather than passes.
